faults.fault: Wall budget gives a 0.5 mm pillar dielectric, but the baseline capacitance (443 fF) and 1 mN change use a 200 um gap; with 0.5 mm the baseline is ~177 fF and the 1 mN change ~2.2 fF (still above the step, but the stated numbers do not follow from the stated stack).
faults.checked_by: recomputed eps0*2.5*4mm2/gap for 200 um and 0.5 mm

faults.fault: Shear differential of 1.22 fF is computed for a 5 um shift from an unexplained formula (2*110*5/900), while the design's own shear-shift number is 77.5 um at 0.5 mN; '1.22 fF/mN' is just a relabel. Shear sensitivity at 1 mN is unsupported.
faults.checked_by: compared the two shear lines; recomputed shift 0.5mN/(pi a^2)*2mm/32.4kPa = 77.5 um

faults.where: How it works / Constraint check: slip
faults.fault: Claims a 1 kHz vibration tap, but the only sensor is the 24-taxel array with a 12 ms full scan (~83 Hz) and no separate vibration element is listed; slip warning rests on an assumed friction coefficient (0.5) and the simulation line is incoherent (warning at 84 ms vs 64 ms fall time to 20 mm).
faults.checked_by: recomputed scan rate 1/12 ms and fall times sqrt(2h/g) = 14.3 ms and 64 ms

Load from the tip reaches the core only through the side walls.
faults.checked_by: measured pillar height against the ~2 mm inset scale bar; compared with stack list

faults.fault: Flange shows four screws whose threaded ends stick down beside the base cylinder into nothing; text says two M2 screws. Callout 6 'rigid domed core' sits on the lower cylinder, not the dome.
Shear-shift calc uses a 2 mm Ecoflex layer, while the stack lists a 1.0 mm skin; local Hertz shear stress applied uniformly through the layer.
Margins (22.7x, 5x) are taken over the converter LSB (0.244 fF = 16 pF/2^16), not over its noise; noise is never estimated.

Shear limit uses 22 N pinch while the screw check uses 35 N; inputs inconsistent (conservative). Location 'to 1 mm' claimed, not computed. Ground textile in stack but not in parts; step 2 panel missing.

C1.why: Fingertip size by arithmetic (15 mm) and 1 mN by a computed capacitance chain that still holds when I correct the gap; margin is over the LSB, not noise.

C2.why: Capacitive micro-pillar normal/shear sensing is a working principle, but the slip channel has no fast sensor and the drawn layer stack has a load-path gap.

C3.why: Many numbers recompute exactly (Hertz 0.356 mm, 2.51 kPa, 443 fF, 22.3 N/mm2), but gap, shear signal and slip timing contradict their own inputs.

C4.why: Labelled cut-away is readable, but flat flex over a hollow dome, oversized pillars and ~11 mm width contradict the text.

C5.why: Buildable from cast silicone and printed core; risks named; LSB presented as a detection floor overstates margins.

C6.why: Sum/difference capacitance idea is stated, but text is dense pipeline jargon and slip mechanism is vague.

C7.why: Four steps with materials (Ecoflex, Dragon Skin, PLA, two screws); few dimensions or bonding details.

C8.why: Clean render; only screws ending in air and chaotic pillar bending.

b2.better_why: Narrowly C: its working principle and explanation are clearest and its risks honest, while A's careful arithmetic is undercut by internal contradictions (gap, shear, slip rate) and a picture that disagrees with its stack; B's picture contradicts its text throughout.

faults.fault: Never checks comfort ('No criteria were given') although the task asks for a comfortable level; its own dense-crowd result 0.545 m/s2 exceeds the usual 0.5 m/s2 maximum-comfort limit unremarked, and that value is read exactly at 1.9 Hz between the split peaks; the peak over frequency is ~0.69 m/s2.
faults.checked_by: 2-DOF frequency sweep with its M, zeta, m, f_t, zeta_t, 280 N

faults.fault: '5.29 equivalent pedestrians' is not derived; it matches 10.8*sqrt(0.004*60), i.e. a sparse 0.5 p/m2 crowd, not a dense one (1.85*sqrt(120) ~ 20), and is applied as a point force at midspan; bare 9.26 m/s2 (~1 g) is not credible.
Damping listed as 0.0956 but 0.0933 used for the 1090 N s/m dashpot; Den Hartog gives 0.0933.
20 t modal mass is an assumption with no deck mass per metre given; no modal test before tuning.
Risks section is empty (detuning, stroke limits, clamp fatigue, other modes not discussed).

By the 500 mm bar the main girders are ~0.15-0.25 m deep, far too shallow for a 40 m span at 1.9 Hz; the mass block is ~1.3 m long by the bar but ~3 m by the person in the step panels; a solid steel block of either size weighs well over 500 kg (~0.064 m3 needed).
faults.checked_by: pixel measurement vs scale bar and silhouette; 500/7850

C3.why: Modal stiffness, TMD stiffness, dashpot, sag and single-walker response all recompute; crowd model and at-1.9-Hz reading are flawed.

faults.fault: +/-60 mm from 7 mm x 6 = 42 mm does not follow, and uses the pre-TMD deck amplitude; with the TMD acting, stroke is ~3 mm at its own 2.0 m/s2 bare level (stops oversized, harmless).
Dashpot coefficient not given; citation markers empty ('precedent .').
Dashpots run diagonally from the girder brackets to the TMD frame's own corner, not to the moving mass, so as drawn they damp nothing; text says they dissipate the mass motion.
Deck slab drawn with a broken, scooped notch under the orange arrow and odd cruciform blocks through the slab, reading as a cut deck against 'no change from the deck'.
Four springs drawn per unit (8 total) versus four spring packs total in the text; an extra mass-like block outside the left frame.

C1.why: Addresses span, mode, comfort and appearance explicitly; comfort result rests on an assumed bare level.

C2.why: Twin Den Hartog TMDs with guides and stops are a proven, workable fix.

C3.why: mu 4.5%, 1.82 Hz, 12.2%, 66 kN/m, 74 mm sag all recompute; the response level is assumed and stroke reasoning loose.

C4.why: Shows twin guided spring-mass units under the deck, but dashpots bypass the mass, the deck looks cut and nothing is labelled or scaled.

C5.why: Modal test first, tuning range, redundancy, inspection; honest about assumptions.

C6.why: Clear plain explanation of out-of-phase masses and peak splitting.

C7.why: Four stages with access, fabrication, clamping and tuning detail.
